_ai_authoring_guide.purpose: Create adult-appropriate, actively constructed English grammar in the Sblocco Learning Studio, from A1 through C1. This is a completed example AND a self-contained AI authoring guide.
pedagogical_rules: Start with a precise sentence-construction skill, not a game theme.
Teach form, meaning and use; do not rely on trigger words or isolated gap filling.
Vary mental operations: build, negate, question, combine, change meaning, edit and explain.
Use realistic adult contexts and provide explicit example(s), anticipated errors and transfer into independent speaking.
Different CEFR levels require different kinds of grammatical decisions, not the same activity with harder vocabulary.
Provide Italian scaffolding only where helpful; preserve accurate natural English.
Make oral tasks truly open-ended and teacher-led, not automatically marked against a single model sentence.
Use multiple valid accepted_answers for constrained typed tasks; if legitimate outputs are too numerous, use oral mode.
Include one or more genuine spoken production tasks with a new context and no mandatory grammar prompt.
Explain why the grammar works and what meaning it communicates. Avoid busywork and empty generic questions.

supported_blocks.purpose: Construct sentences by moving chunks, typing a constrained answer or producing orally
Recall grammar and reflect on independent production

grammar_construction_modes.validation: At least two chunks, already in correct order; omit punctuation from chunks and use terminal_punctuation separately.
At least one correct answer and every defensible constrained variant; automatic checking only for objectively constrained tasks.
Teacher-led and deliberately ungraded; use for open-ended communicative production.

_ai_authoring_guide.import_policy: JSON imports are normalized and become repairable Studio drafts. Never bypass Studio preflight or publish structurally invalid activities.
_ai_authoring_guide.feedback_rule: Correct answers and explanations for independent tasks are revealed according to the activity's configured feedback timing. Teacher notes must remain private.
_ai_authoring_guide.version_info: Grammar in Action kit v1; Studio authoring contract v1; Block Registry v7.

activity.internal_title: A1 · Present Simple · Build Statements & Questions

blocks.title: Subject, verb and the auxiliary
blocks.body: I work in a café. She works in a café. Does she work in a café? She doesn't work on Sundays. The auxiliary does carries third-person agreement; the main verb stays in its base form.

blocks.title: Two kinds of question
blocks.body: Ordinary questions with be invert be and the subject; other present-simple questions use do/does.

blocks.title: Build an affirmative statement
blocks.prompt: Say what Lara usually does before work.
blocks.context: Lara: drinks coffee before work most days.
blocks.explanation: Third-person singular uses drinks; usually precedes the main verb.
blocks.teacher_note: Ask the student to change Lara to I.

blocks.title: Form a question
blocks.prompt: Ask whether Lara works on Sundays.

blocks.title: Negate the sentence
blocks.prompt: Rewrite exactly as a negative: Lara works on Sundays.
accepted_answers: Lara does not work on Sundays.
blocks.explanation: The main verb is work, not works, after doesn't.

blocks.title: Use grammar in real speaking
blocks.prompt: Ask your teacher three questions about their normal week. Then say what you learned using complete sentences.
blocks.context: Ask about work, hobbies and weekends.
blocks.learner_hint: Do you…? / Where do you…? / What time do you…?
blocks.teacher_note: Correct the question word order aloud. Ask for an independent reformulation at the end.
